title: Follow the Pauli
lesson: Gates transform a check as it moves through the circuit.
brief: You can start only Z checks. Place one before different gates and watch how the game calculates its end edge. The end edge is determined by the gates inside the check's span.
learning_moment: The check's start and end edges must describe the same measurement carried through the intervening gates. The game calculates this transformation for you. For example, H swaps X and Z; S maps X to Y (and maps Y to −X); CNOT can spread an X from its control to its target and a Z from its target back to its control. The mathematical rule is U P U†, but you can learn the behavior by watching the edge change. If a check ends at the final readout and its end edge contains only Z and identity, it may be merged into the measured parity without extra end-edge gates.
hint: Start a Z check on q1 just before its H gate. Drag its end to different slots and watch the end edge change. Try the same around S and CNOT. To meet the goal, find an end edge that is Z only at the last slot.
reflection: Which gates changed the Pauli between the start and end edges?
noise_note: The model spreads errors across the gates using the same base rates.

explanation: Watch how one Pauli changes: H turns Z into X, the CNOT copies the X onto q1, the H on q1 turns that X back into Z, and S leaves Z alone. The final H on q0 turns its X into Z.
So a Z on q0 at slot 0 ends at the readout as Z on q0 and q1, asking whether q0 and q1 agree, which every correct result does.
Starting on q1 before its H instead ends with a Y in the end edge, which cannot use the final readout.
